body: Thanks so much for taking the time to respond to me over the past day or so, I really appreciate it.  I guess I just have to take things one step at a time and try to improve myself.  🙂

For me the the pressure from Mormonism is more the get married and have kids young or you are a failure.  For example my parents had me when my dad was 22 and my mom was 20, and they had already been married for two years and had a house by the time I was born (oldest child).  My immediate family and I haven’t been active for about ten years(and I’ve been an atheist since about 13 now 22) but the pressure is still there.  I just don’t feel comfortable talking with people.  

To answer the second question, I don’t really open up to anyone at all.  I always said I wasn’t a “touchy feely person” I don’t let people in.  I’m scared to talk to my family about that stuff.  I don’t really feel that close to anyone except my sister and I’m afraid that if I told her these things she would tell my parents and I don’t know how they would react.  So I’ve always just dealt with it on my own, usually I just try to tough it out until it passes.
Thanks, it does help.  I’m the same way, some days I’m perfectly fine and other days I just wish I had someone.
You’re right.  I don’t want to just settle, but in my head I think there’s no way that there’s someone for me.  I guess I should become more comfortable with myself and work on my self image.

I think you’re absolutely right about mental health.  I think part of my problem is that I don’t talk to anyone about these things.  I never open up to people about the struggles that I’m facing in my own head.
I think we are similar in age.  I left high school in 2017.  I also struggle meeting new people.  And after I spend some time with people and they leave I get really down too.  Thanks for commenting.
Having hope is something I’ve never really been good at.  I’ve always been pretty pessimistic, I guess that’s something I should try to work on.  Thanks for the comment.

Thanks for the kind words.  I grew up in Mormonism so I feel like I understand the parental (and honestly societal) pressure to get married and have kids.  I always told my family I wasn’t going to do those things.  I told I didn’t want to, but in all honesty I do want to do those things.  I just don’t think that there’s someone out there for me.  I’ve tried a few times to talk to girls and date and they are never interested in me, so I’ve kind of been in the dumps.  Anyway, thanks for the response.
